#### 1. hypermetabolism due to uncoupled mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1268020)

**Proposed mechanism:** Causal variant in SLC25A4 (null) —LEADS_TO→ SLC25A4 (HGNC:10877); SLC25A4 (HGNC:10877) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0042754); Causal variant in ATP5F1B (null) —LEADS_TO→ ATP5F1B (HGNC:7362); ATP5F1B (HGNC:7362) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0042754); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0042754) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive external ophthalmoplegia (HP:0003743); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0042754) —LEADS_TO→ Elevated basal metabolic rate (HP:0002174). Mutations in SLC25A4 lead to impaired mitochondrial ATP synthesis, causing progressive external ophthalmoplegia. Similarly, mutations in ATP5F1B also disrupt mitochondrial ATP synthesis, leading to a hypermetabolic state due to uncoupling. The shared convergence point is the disruption of mitochondrial ATP synthesis.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if genetic analysis reveals that the causal variants for disease A consistently map to genes unrelated to mitochondrial ATP synthesis, or if the causal variants for disease B do not impact the mitochondrial ATP synthesis pathway. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in gnomAD within the coding regions of SLC25A4 or ATP5F1B that are not associated with either disease would weaken the claim of these specific genes being the sole causal agents.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on mitochondrial ATP synthesis as a mechanistic link could reveal common therapeutic targets or strategies for managing both progressive external ophthalmoplegia and metabolic disorders associated with mitochondrial dysfunction.
